415439.title: Harp Run with Wind Chimes and Birds.wav
415439.description:
Melodic Snippets from recordings of me playing the Swar SanGam. This wonderful instrument is a combination of the Swarmandal and the Tampura. 15 harp strings and 4 Drone/Bass strings. 
In these recordings I am only using the Swarmandal (Harp) part.
It is tuned to C sharp, but I have dropped the fourth note (F sharp) out of the scale.

There are four packs with lots of recordings in them, strums, plucks, short improvisations. 
"Short melodic statements" are 1-2 bars. "Riffs" are 2-4 bars. "Melodies" are about 30 seconds and "Runs and Flutters" speaks for itself. There is recording of tuning up the Swarmandal in the melodies pack.

The snippets were taken from recordings done on three different days so you may notice a slight difference in volume and background noise. A couple of the recordings have some ambient noise (bird tweets, wind chimes,)
Some of the melodies are based around a similar theme but have enough variation to be interesting/useful.

Credit is not required but always appreciated. Linking to the sound allows others to find this amazing website. :-)
I love to hear what you have used my sounds for!

397657.title: MachineGunloop.wav
397657.description:
Made in Ableton live this time, it is a multilayered loop consisting of recordings of an ak47, a 30 caliber 1918, and an m60 machine gun to make a rediculous powerful sound.

A very short clicky kick drum with the high end reduced is added before the initial gunshot to make it punch more, otherwise it would sound weaker. There are two mechanical bolt sounds, one covering the upper mid range, and the other covering the extreme highs.

Shell ejections and two reverb tails were mixed in at the end with some simple automated panning to make it move around the stereo field.

The tempo slowly decreases to simulate barrel heating

Lots of processing. The layers were eq'ed, then ran into a software amp that is gently distorting the low and mid range. Then smashed together with OTT multiband upward/downward compression to bring out the details.

A maximizer was used to bring up the loudness some.


enjoy

413738.title: wing-beat great spotted woodpecker.wav
413738.description:
Wing-beat great spotted woodpecker. Recorded on 20m.

The great spotted woodpecker has a powerful, undulating flight, where the wings are practically not lifted above the horizontal plane. With every 3rd wing beat, the wings are held still for a moment against the body, so that a kind of rhythm is created which causes the undulating flight. One, two, three, hop; one, two, three, hup. At hip the body goes up to the height, to descend in a curve. A new wing beat then gives an upward rise again. 
 Here you can hear the one, two, three wing beat. Not a great recording cause it was just by-catch of a longer nature recording.

410832.description:
I tried to reproduce the sound of ocean waves crashing crashing onto a shore. I didn't use any recorded sound to make it. Firstly, I generated a pink noise. I then edited its dynamic so that the sound would fade in and out slowly. I repeated this sample 4 times, and added a small phaser effect to add variation to the sound, as well as a little reverb. I made sure that the whole sample would loop. 
Behind this, I added a quiet rose noise to simulate the constant noise of the ocean.

________________________

410762.title: GODIN_Cassie_2017_2018_Microwave.wav
410762.description:
Goal: to create a real sound of a microwave without a microwave.

Production steps: I recorded an alarm clock and a sound of vacuum cleaner. Then, I added on the sound track of the vacuum cleaner four alarm sounds: one at the very beginning, then three at the end. I extended the last ring so it really gives an impression of microwave that rings. To finish, I modulated the amplification, the bass and the treble until it sounds like a real microwave.

• Typologie (Cf. Pierre Schaeffer) : X et quadruple N’
• Morphologie (Cf. Pierre Schaeffer) :
1. Masse : groupe de sons cannelés.
2. Timbre harmonique : le timbre harmonique est relativement terne, les seules hauteurs sont les sonneries qui ne permettent pas de « donner vie » au son.
3. Grain : rugueux.
4. Allure : sans vibrato mais l'allure paraît lourde.
5. Dynamique : abrupte en longueur.
6. Profil mélodique : si le fond est plutôt glissant, les variations faites par les sonneries sont quant à elles scalaires.
7. Profil de masse :
- site : accentuation sur les sonneries.
- calibre : équalisation sur le fond sonore (aspirateur).

410763.title: GODIN_Cassie_2017_2018_EnteringADungeon.wav
410763.description:
Goal: to remind someone knocking on a door and entering a dungeon.

Production steps:  I recorded someone knocking and opening a door, then I accelerated the speed and lowered the height. I also added reverb so that the effect would be more terrifying and would really remind a big door leading to a scary place.

• Typologie (Cf. Pierre Schaeffer) : X’’ puis V
• Morphologie (Cf. Pierre Schaeffer) :
1. Masse : groupe de sons cannelés.
2. Timbre harmonique : le timbre est plat et sombre, notamment grâce à l'effet réverbération.
3. Grain : rugueux.
4. Allure : sans vibrato mais l'allure paraît lourde.
5. Dynamique : la dynamique est très abrupte à cause des coups frappés à la porte dès les premières secondes.
6. Profil mélodique : les variations (ici, les coups frappés à la porte) sont scalaires, seule la fin est serpentine.
7. Profil de masse :
- site : accentuation sur les coups frappés afin que ceux-ci soit mis en avant.
- calibre : équalisation pour le fond sonore.

410761.title: GODIN_Cassie_2017_2018_StressfulAtmosphere.wav
410761.description:
Goal: to create a creepy atmosphere with a weird melody and crows' cawing.

Production steps: I recorded several Larsen effects and generated sounds in very high frequencies, which I joined to each other until I got a certain melody. Then, I added a Paulstrech effect and increased the reverb several times. When the music seemed quite stressful, I added crows' sounds recorded outside (and augmented by amplification) at the very end of the melody. I copied and pasted the melody because I thought it sounded better played twice.

• Typologie (Cf. Pierre Schaeffer) : V
• Morphologie (Cf. Pierre Schaeffer) :
1. Masse : groupe nodal.
2. Timbre harmonique : acide, aigre, donnant une ambiance presque électrisante.
3. Grain : rugueux.
4. Allure : sans vibrato avec une allure presque stressante.
5. Dynamique : douce et graduelle.
6. Profil mélodique : les variations sont serpentines, la seule hauteur presque « dérangeante » pour l'oreille est due aux croassements de corbeaux.
7. Profil de masse :
- site : simple accentuation sur les croassements.
- calibre : une équalisation a été réalisée pour réaliser une mélodie plus équilibrée et serpentine.

426165.title: M224 Mortar Impact  Distant 02
426165.description:
Recorded roughly 900m from the source. This is the report of the impact/explosion.

These sounds were recorded via a Sony HD Handycam around 2007/2008 in Iraq while participating in the so-called 'global war on terror.' I was not a mortarman but was part of the security detail working with them. We utilized indirect fires several times, some of which were controlled situations where I was able to record video.

These sounds were extracted from said video, and are of limited quality because of it. I am not an expert on these weapons systems, so if my nomenclatures are slightly off, or my description isn't perfectly accurate, forgive me.

Please send me a message if you use these sounds in a project. They are free, and the only thing I get out of the deal is the satisfaction of seeing them used in some creative work.

415440.title: Harp Melodic Wild Run Down.wav
415440.description:
Melodic Snippets from recordings of me playing the Swar SanGam. This wonderful instrument is a combination of the Swarmandal and the Tampura. 15 harp strings and 4 Drone/Bass strings. 
In these recordings I am only using the Swarmandal (Harp) part.
It is tuned to C sharp, but I have dropped the fourth note (F sharp) out of the scale.

There are four packs with lots of recordings in them, strums, plucks, short improvisations. 
"Short melodic statements" are 1-2 bars. "Riffs" are 2-4 bars. "Melodies" are about 30 seconds and "Runs and Flutters" speaks for itself. There is recording of tuning up the Swarmandal in the melodies pack.

The snippets were taken from recordings done on three different days so you may notice a slight difference in volume and background noise. A couple of the recordings have some ambient noise (bird tweets, wind chimes,)
Some of the melodies are based around a similar theme but have enough variation to be interesting/useful.

Credit is not required but always appreciated. Linking to the sound allows others to find this amazing website. :-)
I love to hear what you have used my sounds for!

410393.title: PANTIGNY_JeanLoup_2017_2018_droplets.wav
410393.description:
This loop was 100% created in Audacity. I created a sinusoïdal chirp (starting frequency ~400hz, ending frequency ~800hz), and edited its profile so that it would fade in very quickly and fade out slowly. I added some reverb to reproduce the sound that a drop of water would make in a bathroom. I repeated the sound and made sure that it would loop perfectly. 

---

Typologie/morphologie de P. Schaeffer

Ce son est une série d'impulsions variées (V')

Masse : C'est un son seul dont la fréquence varie rapidement. 

Grain : Le son est lisse (Sinusoïde)

Dynamique : L'attaque du son est assez abrupte, suivi d'un peak très rapide et d'un relâchement plus lent

Profil mélodique : La variation de fréquence est serpentine.

410391.title: PANTIGNY_JeanLoup_2017_2018_glassOfWater.wav
410391.description:
In order to create this sound, I recorded myself pouring water into a glass. I then reduced the ambient noise in Audacity.

--- 

Typologie/morphologie de P. Schaeffer

Le bruit étant un assez chaotique, je le qualifierai de continu complexe (X). Cependant, on entend une variation dans la fréquence lors du remplissage, ce qui pourrait aussi être interprété comme un son continu varié (V)

Masse : Il s'agit d'un son seul complexe. 

Timbre harmonique : Je trouve ce son est assez brillant et cristallin. 

Grain : Le son n'est pas lisse, cependant il n'est pas non plus rugueux. On pourrait parler d'un grain de frottement. 

Allure : On entend un vibrato dans la fréquence.

Dynamique : Le profil dynamique de ce son est assez régulier, avec une attaque douce, un long sutain et un relâchement doux. 

Profil mélodique : La variation de fréquence est serpentine.

410390.title: PANTIGNY_JeanLoup_2017_2018_heartbeatBreath.wav
410390.description:
The heartbeat loop was 100% generated in Audacity.

In order to do it, I generated a chirp (Sifflet in french) with a starting frequency of 100hz and and ending frequency of 1hz.
The amplitude was also reduced from 0.75 to 0. The duration of this chirp was set to 0.5 seconds.
To make the second part of the heartbeat, I generated another chirp, with a higher starting frequency, a lower amplitude at the start and a duration of 0.25 seconds.
I shifted the second chirp so that the two chirps simulated a full heart beat.
I then added some silence at the end of the cycle, and then I repeated the cycle 10 times. 
I added some reverb and augmented the bass (as well as lowering the treble) to smooth the sound and make it sound like a deep heartbeat.

I recorded myself breathing, and I added this sound while making sure that 3 respiration cycles would perfectly align with 11 heartbeats, in order to make a perfect loop.

--- 

Typologie/morphologie de P. Schaeffer

Le battement de cœur est une impulsion variée (V'). Étant simplement répété et ne variant pas au fur et à mesure des répétitions, on ne peut pas selon moi qualifier cette boucle d'itération variée (V'')

Masse : Ce sample est composé de sons cannelés. En effet on entend la hauteur du son des battements de cœur, mais la respiration (son complexe) s'ajoute par dessus. 

Grain : Le grain du son du battement de cœur est très lisse car purement sinusoïdale, cependant le souffle par dessus est lui rugueux. 

Dynamique : Les battements de cœur ont une attaque assez abrupte suivie de deux pics et d'un relâchement immédiat. Le souffle quand à lui à une attaque assez douce, une longue phase de sustain et un relâchement lui aussi doux. 

Profil mélodique : La transition entre les deux notes qui composent le battement de cœur est assez scalaire. 

Profil de masse : Les battements de cœur ainsi que le souffle sont d'un niveau sonore similaire, cependant les battements de cœur sont bien plus graves.

410825.title: COVINI_Jessica_2017_2018_Tsunami.wav
410825.description:
Tsunami in Japan was created with a mix of recorded songs and also the creation of several tracks. 

First I generated 3 differents noises (I changed the height of the first one by reducing 2 times 30 half tons, I increased the height at the end for the second one and reduced a little the height of the third noise). I finished by adding reverb (60%) used "Wah Wah" effect and fade out. By doing this, I got the saturation that I wanted, creating the impression of the sound of a real tsunami.

After I used registered songs of seagulls, waves and sirens. I added reverb (39%) for all of my tracks and repeated the song of the siren 3 times. I also used the effect "normalisation" and used the effect "noise decrease" and fade in. I wanted that when the tsunami arrives, the sound looks like an explosion.
Description: Everything was perfect and quiet in this small island of Japan, the beach, the sound of the seagulls ... when suddenly we can hear the trembling sound of sirens. Yes, the tsunami is here, ready to destroy everything.

---

Descriptif selon la typologie de Schaeffer :
Typologie : continu complexe (X) 
Masse : Groupe nodal avec sons complexes)
Timbre harmonique : acide, doux, puis granuleux et terne 
Grain : Le son est plutôt lisse au départ puis rugueux à la fin
Allure : Pas de vibrato
Dynamique : Attaque douce et graduelle  
Profil mélodique : Variation serpentine
Profil de masse : Site pour le son d'ambiance, qui apporte plus de profondeur. Calibre : pour l'équalisation utilisée pour nettoyer les fréquences perturbatrices (sons indésirables) et mettre en avant les éléments voulus.

410827.title: COVINI_Jessica_2017_2018_Corridors.wav
410827.description:
Corridors is an ambient sound created with a mix of recorded songs in order to create an atmosphere of a classic corridor in college.

I used the sound of someone who is walking, repeated the sound and add reverb. I also add the sound of a smartphone (ringtone + writing messages) and someone knocking on the door where I added reverb (60%) and the Paulstrech effect on both of them to create a better immersion. I optimized the result by adding the sound of a door, add again some reverb (40%) and by low or high pitching them. I also used fade in and fade out and used the effect "noise decrease" for a better immersion.

---

Description: An ambient sound in college (12 seconds).

415413.title: Harp Strumming Riff 1.wav
415413.description:
Melodic Snippets from recordings of me playing the Swar SanGam. This wonderful instrument is a combination of the Swarmandal and the Tampura. 15 harp strings and 4 Drone/Bass strings. 
In these recordings I am only using the Swarmandal (Harp) part.
It is tuned to C sharp, but I have dropped the fourth note (F sharp) out of the scale.

There are four packs with lots of recordings in them, strums, plucks, short improvisations. 
"Short melodic statements" are 1-2 bars. "Riffs" are 2-4 bars. "Melodies" are about 30 seconds and "Runs and Flutters" speaks for itself. There is recording of tuning up the Swarmandal in the melodies pack.

The snippets were taken from recordings done on three different days so you may notice a slight difference in volume and background noise. A couple of the recordings have some ambient noise (bird tweets, wind chimes,)
Some of the melodies are based around a similar theme but have enough variation to be interesting/useful.

Credit is not required but always appreciated. Linking to the sound allows others to find this amazing website. :-)
I love to hear what you have used my sounds for!

404317.title: Rain heard 900 meters below the sea surface
404317.description: This recording of rainfall on the sea surface, as heard at a depth of 900 m, is part of a series of recordings from an oceanic soundscape project using a deep-sea cabled observatory off the California coast. The first segment is the background sound before the rain squall; the second segment is during the squall. More information about this research project is available in a publication. The fact that rain falling on the sea surface can be heard in the deep sea illustrates the efficacy of sound as a carrier of information in the sea, where it travels orders of magnitude farther than light. The recording was made on 21 March 2016. © 2016 Monterey Bay Aquarium Research Institute

395409.title: Laugh Track 2.mp3
395409.description:
Apparently I made this for my animation which supposedly a parody of sitcom shows...and since I find the laugh tracks in the internet a little too "cliche" (and I've used it a bunch of times in my videos already), I decided to make my own.

So, all I did was record my voice doing different kinds of laughing (mostly giggles or chuckles since I somehow can't force out a fake laughter by the time of recording) in my normal and falsetto voice for at least 1 minute. Then I edited it all out in Audacity. I also resampled older recordings of my fake laughters and pitched down the duplicated tracks so that it would sound "bigger".

Pardon for that tiny screech sound toward the end as I never silenced out the background noises of the audios.

Please credit me as LittleRainySeasons if you're going to use them. Thanks :)

396795.title: Distant Huge Explosion.wav
396795.description:
I went to Audacity and recorded silence from my laptop mic because I got bored, and I realized that there's always a 'click' hearable at the beginning of every laptop recording. So I added some reverb to this click purely out of boredom and it actually ended up sounding somewhat like a distant explosion. Then I suddenly got this marvelous idea to process it into an actual explosion sound and just upload it on here!

After putting the reverb on the click sound, I pitched it down, then did some EQ'ing by getting rid of some of the highs and adding some lows to it, then did some more tweaking to it until I ended up with this final sound. Let me know what you think!

415429.title: Harp Tinkly Riff 1.wav
415429.description:
Melodic Snippets from recordings of me playing the Swar SanGam. This wonderful instrument is a combination of the Swarmandal and the Tampura. 15 harp strings and 4 Drone/Bass strings. 
In these recordings I am only using the Swarmandal (Harp) part.
It is tuned to C sharp, but I have dropped the fourth note (F sharp) out of the scale.

There are four packs with lots of recordings in them, strums, plucks, short improvisations. 
"Short melodic statements" are 1-2 bars. "Riffs" are 2-4 bars. "Melodies" are about 30 seconds and "Runs and Flutters" speaks for itself. There is recording of tuning up the Swarmandal in the melodies pack.

The snippets were taken from recordings done on three different days so you may notice a slight difference in volume and background noise. A couple of the recordings have some ambient noise (bird tweets, wind chimes,)
Some of the melodies are based around a similar theme but have enough variation to be interesting/useful.

Credit is not required but always appreciated. Linking to the sound allows others to find this amazing website. :-)
I love to hear what you have used my sounds for!

387479.description:
I did the sound design for a short film where one character threw darts at another character while they stood against a wall, we went out and did some audio recording for the sequence using a at875r mic and a zoom h4n to record the audio of darts hitting things, I think we ended up layering in a number of different sounds to make a nice set of dart sounds

This sound effect is part of the filmmakers archive

www.thefilmmakersarchive.com

The archive is my current hobby, I hope to bring a collection of free creative commons sound FX and Music to creators like myself for their own projects. check it out if you need some FX or music for more projects in the future (as a note most of the sound FX in the archive can be found here on free sound, the music of course not so much)

~Dane S Casperson

407688.title: Male - Chewing and Swallowing (Peanuts)
407688.description:
The sound of peanuts being chewed and swallowed. The sound of the plastic packet that they are contained in crinkling can briefly be heard in the background at the 3 - 5-second mark. The chewing was done as open-mouthed as possible to capture as much of the eating process as possible, as well as the rubbery squeaks of teeth colliding against the peanuts' exterior. 

Recorded on a Rode NT1A.

407685.title: Male Burp (Soda)
407685.description:
The sound of a male burping as a result of drinking soda. Short and stifled at first but then at the 4-second mark, a somewhat visceral and elongated one emerges. 

I'm sorry in advance for what you're going to hear. It's gross, man. 

Recorded on a Rode NT1A

396325.title: SemiAutoRifle1
396325.description:
A semi-automatic rifle, pitched down 3 semi-tones

Made in bitwig, i used 10 different recorded gunshot layers that have been eq'ed and multiband compressed to form a new gun sound. Subbass was synthesized for the super low end. 

The process i use is to select frequencies using high pass and lowpass filters from a recording for the lows, mids and highs. This forms a "layered sound"

396327.title: SemiAutoRifle3
396327.description:
A semi-automatic rifle, unpitched

Made in bitwig, i used 10 different recorded gunshot layers that have been eq'ed and multiband compressed to form a new gun sound. Subbass was synthesized for the super low end. 

The process i use is to select frequencies using high pass and lowpass filters from a recording for the lows, mids and highs. This forms a "layered sound" 


A kick drum was put before the initial gunshot to give it punch and make it sound larger.

415475.title: Harp Short 22.wav
415475.description:
Melodic Snippets from recordings of me playing the Swar SanGam. This wonderful instrument is a combination of the Swarmandal and the Tampura. 15 harp strings and 4 Drone/Bass strings. 
In these recordings I am only using the Swarmandal (Harp) part.
It is tuned to C sharp, but I have dropped the fourth note (F sharp) out of the scale.

There are four packs with lots of recordings in them, strums, plucks, short improvisations. 
"Short melodic statements" are 1-2 bars. "Riffs" are 2-4 bars. "Melodies" are about 30 seconds and "Runs and Flutters" speaks for itself. There is recording of tuning up the Swarmandal in the melodies pack.

The snippets were taken from recordings done on three different days so you may notice a slight difference in volume and background noise. A couple of the recordings have some ambient noise (bird tweets, wind chimes,)
Some of the melodies are based around a similar theme but have enough variation to be interesting/useful.

Credit is not required but always appreciated. Linking to the sound allows others to find this amazing website. :-)
I love to hear what you have used my sounds for!

415387.title: Harp Melody 2.wav
415387.description:
Melodic Snippets from recordings of me playing the Swar SanGam. This wonderful instrument is a combination of the Swarmandal and the Tanpura. 15 harp strings and 4 Drone/Bass strings. 
In these recordings I am only using the Swarmandal (Harp) part.
It is tuned to C sharp, but I have dropped the fourth note (F sharp) out of the scale.

There are four packs with lots of recordings in them; strums, plucks, short improvisations. 
"Short melodic statements" are 1-2 bars. "Riffs" are 2-4 bars. "Melodies" are about 30 seconds and "Runs and Flutters" is experimenting with running up and down the strings. There is recording of tuning up the Swarmandal in the melodies pack.

The snippets were taken from recordings done on three different days so you may notice a slight difference in volume and background noise. A couple of the recordings have some ambient noise (bird tweets, wind chimes,)
Some of the melodies are based around a similar theme but have enough variation to be interesting/useful.

Credit is not required but always appreciated. Linking to the sound allows others to find this amazing website. :-) 
I love to hear what you have used my sounds for!

410879.title: CHAMBLAS_Andrea_2017_2018_slotmachine.wav
410879.description:
I recorded the sound of a coffee machine; In audacity, I reducted the noise to 26db, sensibility to 10 and frequency to 12, then I compressed the sound (threshold-20db, level of noise 40, ratio 3:1 and attacks: 0.10 dry)
The, I offset the gain to 0db after compression and I normalized by deleting any gap cc, and finally, I normalized the amplitude to -7.5db. I obtained a warmer and clearer sound, without noise in the background. I deleted the part with the coffee and only kept the part with money, so it looks like a slot machine in casinos. I didn't add special effects because I think this realistic sound is already interesting to use as it is.

Code typologie de Schaeffler : X' / X''
Masse : son cannelés avec mélange de sons complexes et de sons toniques  (avec des hauteurs de note)
Timbre harmonique : terne 
Grain : rugueux
Allure : pas de vibrato
Dynamique : l'attaque est plutôt douce et graduelle
Profil mélodique : variations plutôt scalaires
Profil de masse : calibre : présence d'un "filtrage", d'une équalisation

415415.title: Harp Strumming Riff 5.wav
415415.description:
Melodic Snippets from recordings of me playing the Swar SanGam. This wonderful instrument is a combination of the Swarmandal and the Tampura. 15 harp strings and 4 Drone/Bass strings. 
In these recordings I am only using the Swarmandal (Harp) part.
It is tuned to C sharp, but I have dropped the fourth note (F sharp) out of the scale.

There are four packs with lots of recordings in them, strums, plucks, short improvisations. 
"Short melodic statements" are 1-2 bars. "Riffs" are 2-4 bars. "Melodies" are about 30 seconds and "Runs and Flutters" speaks for itself. There is recording of tuning up the Swarmandal in the melodies pack.

The snippets were taken from recordings done on three different days so you may notice a slight difference in volume and background noise. A couple of the recordings have some ambient noise (bird tweets, wind chimes,)
Some of the melodies are based around a similar theme but have enough variation to be interesting/useful.

Credit is not required but always appreciated. Linking to the sound allows others to find this amazing website. :-)
I love to hear what you have used my sounds for!

404905.title: Large Green Sawfly Larvae 02.m4a
404905.description: Group of large green sawfly larvae, indoors on a 3mm melamine board. About 50 individuals were in the group, recorded with a Rode NT55 mic on a Marantz PMD661, 13 October 2017, 3:01PM. The mic was about 100mm from the group. The larvae make a soft, continuous, hissing/crackling sound, with the occasional thump with their tails to indicate their presence to others in the group. They live on eucalyptus leaves, often descending to the ground and moving in a swarm to another location. Take with a grain of salt anyone who says these larvae strip trees. We've had thousands of these larvae in our yard over the past 30 years, and have never had a problem amongst our dozen or so gum trees. I've also noticed them across the road on young gum trees only 3mm high – and again, little evidence of leaf-stripping. They're a beautiful larvae, a delight to watch, photograph and record. A video of a similar group can be downloaded here: http://www.mediafire.com/file/fhpk3crixndkii3/Vi2192.m4v

415404.title: Harp Lovely Riff.wav
415404.description:
Melodic Snippets from recordings of me playing the Swar SanGam. This wonderful instrument is a combination of the Swarmandal and the Tampura. 15 harp strings and 4 Drone/Bass strings. 
In these recordings I am only using the Swarmandal (Harp) part.
It is tuned to C sharp, but I have dropped the fourth note (F sharp) out of the scale.

There are four packs with lots of recordings in them, strums, plucks, short improvisations. 
"Short melodic statements" are 1-2 bars. "Riffs" are 2-4 bars. "Melodies" are about 30 seconds and "Runs and Flutters" speaks for itself. There is recording of tuning up the Swarmandal in the melodies pack.

The snippets were taken from recordings done on three different days so you may notice a slight difference in volume and background noise. A couple of the recordings have some ambient noise (bird tweets, wind chimes,)
Some of the melodies are based around a similar theme but have enough variation to be interesting/useful.

Credit is not required but always appreciated. Linking to the sound allows others to find this amazing website. :-)
I love to hear what you have used my sounds for!

410757.title: PERRET_Maëlle_2017_2018_bathroom.wav
410757.description:
At the college, we recorded the noise of someone who enter in the bathroom. This person let the water flow. At the same time, she hummed a melody and wash her hands. To conclude the extract, I closed the door. 

After that, I imported the sound in Audacity. I amplified the sound. And then, I added a second sound track in which I recorded my voice. I hummed a melody. But the track wasn't long enough. So I repeated twice the same period. To conclude, as we might be in a enclosed area, I added a reverberation ( 64%) in the first track. 


____ 

Morphologie de Schaeffer : 

Il s'agit d'un objet sonore comportant un son continu varié (V) et un son avec des impulsions toniques (N').

Masse : Mélange de noeuds  ( sons complexes et sons toniques) 

Profil mélodique : serpentine.

410756.title: PERRET_Maëlle_2017_2018_busyline.wav
410756.description:
I generate a new sound track in Audacity. In this track, I added the "wahwah" effect. I changed the tempo, I speeded up at 2 seconds. Then, at 3,5 seconds, I cut the sound. After that, I repeat three times the 3,5 seconds period. 
To conclude, I added a fade out at the end of the track. 


I wanted to create the sound of a busy line. For instance, if the caller is in line with an other person, we can heard a repetitive sound. Here, it's the same process but more acure. 

--- 
Morphologie de Schaeffer: 

Il s'agit d'un objet sonore comportant un son continu varié (V) et un son avec des itérations toniques (V''). 

Masse : groupe nodal 

Grain : robotique 

Dynamique : attaque violente et son en continu 

Profil mélodique : serpentine 

Profil masse : site / recensement de diverses hauteurs de son dans le son global;

395407.title: Laugh Track 4.mp3
395407.description:
Apparently I made this for my animation which supposedly a parody of sitcom shows...and since I find the laugh tracks in the internet a little too "cliche" (and I've used it a bunch of times in my videos already), I decided to make my own.

So, all I did was record my voice doing different kinds of laughing (mostly giggles or chuckles since I somehow can't force out a fake laughter by the time of recording) in my normal and falsetto voice for at least 1 minute. Then I edited it all out in Audacity. I also resampled older recordings of my fake laughters and pitched down the duplicated tracks so that it would sound "bigger".

Please credit me as LittleRainySeasons if you're going to use them. Thanks :)

410754.title: ALEBOYEH_Sanam_2017_2018_Couleur Café.wav
410754.description:
Production steps
This sound reminds  the moment you put coins in the machine to get your coffee.
This is a mixed sound : a audio recording which was modified on Audacity to achieve this effect.

The original sound comes from coins being introduced in the machine. I selected special moments of the recording.

I then added the following effects:
- More bass : +4.0dB
- Tempo : +0.6 beats/minute
Finally I have lengthened the part where the coins were falling to create the impression that there were more of it.

Descriptif et critères morphologiques :
Typologie de Schaeffer : ce son est une itération variée (V’’)
Masse : complexe (non repérable) 
Timbre : sonnant
Grain: faible, plutôt lisse
Allure : semi mécanique semi naturelle (irrégulière ou non selon le moment)
Couleur : métallique
Profil mélodique : scalaire, avec séparations très nettes
Dynamique : abrupte

415443.title: Harp Up Run 2.wav
415443.description:
Melodic Snippets from recordings of me playing the Swar SanGam. This wonderful instrument is a combination of the Swarmandal and the Tampura. 15 harp strings and 4 Drone/Bass strings. 
In these recordings I am only using the Swarmandal (Harp) part.
It is tuned to C sharp, but I have dropped the fourth note (F sharp) out of the scale.

There are four packs with lots of recordings in them, strums, plucks, short improvisations. 
"Short melodic statements" are 1-2 bars. "Riffs" are 2-4 bars. "Melodies" are about 30 seconds and "Runs and Flutters" speaks for itself. There is recording of tuning up the Swarmandal in the melodies pack.

The snippets were taken from recordings done on three different days so you may notice a slight difference in volume and background noise. A couple of the recordings have some ambient noise (bird tweets, wind chimes,)
Some of the melodies are based around a similar theme but have enough variation to be interesting/useful.

Credit is not required but always appreciated. Linking to the sound allows others to find this amazing website. :-)
I love to hear what you have used my sounds for!

415459.title: Harp Short Tinkle 2.wav
415459.description:
Melodic Snippets from recordings of me playing the Swar SanGam. This wonderful instrument is a combination of the Swarmandal and the Tampura. 15 harp strings and 4 Drone/Bass strings. 
In these recordings I am only using the Swarmandal (Harp) part.
It is tuned to C sharp, but I have dropped the fourth note (F sharp) out of the scale.

There are four packs with lots of recordings in them, strums, plucks, short improvisations. 
"Short melodic statements" are 1-2 bars. "Riffs" are 2-4 bars. "Melodies" are about 30 seconds and "Runs and Flutters" speaks for itself. There is recording of tuning up the Swarmandal in the melodies pack.

The snippets were taken from recordings done on three different days so you may notice a slight difference in volume and background noise. A couple of the recordings have some ambient noise (bird tweets, wind chimes,)
Some of the melodies are based around a similar theme but have enough variation to be interesting/useful.

Credit is not required but always appreciated. Linking to the sound allows others to find this amazing website. :-)
I love to hear what you have used my sounds for!

415428.title: Harp Picking and Strumming 8.wav
415428.description:
Melodic Snippets from recordings of me playing the Swar SanGam. This wonderful instrument is a combination of the Swarmandal and the Tampura. 15 harp strings and 4 Drone/Bass strings. 
In these recordings I am only using the Swarmandal (Harp) part.
It is tuned to C sharp, but I have dropped the fourth note (F sharp) out of the scale.

There are four packs with lots of recordings in them, strums, plucks, short improvisations. 
"Short melodic statements" are 1-2 bars. "Riffs" are 2-4 bars. "Melodies" are about 30 seconds and "Runs and Flutters" speaks for itself. There is recording of tuning up the Swarmandal in the melodies pack.

The snippets were taken from recordings done on three different days so you may notice a slight difference in volume and background noise. A couple of the recordings have some ambient noise (bird tweets, wind chimes,)
Some of the melodies are based around a similar theme but have enough variation to be interesting/useful.

Credit is not required but always appreciated. Linking to the sound allows others to find this amazing website. :-)
I love to hear what you have used my sounds for!

426164.title: M224 Mortar Impact Medium Distance 01
426164.description:
Recorded roughly 600m from the source. This is the report of the impact/explosion.

These sounds were recorded via a Sony HD Handycam around 2007/2008 in Iraq while participating in the so-called 'global war on terror.' I was not a mortarman but was part of the security detail working with them. We utilized indirect fires several times, some of which were controlled situations where I was able to record video.

These sounds were extracted from said video, and are of limited quality because of it. I am not an expert on these weapons systems, so if my nomenclatures are slightly off, or my description isn't perfectly accurate, forgive me.

Please send me a message if you use these sounds in a project. They are free, and the only thing I get out of the deal is the satisfaction of seeing them used in some creative work.

415409.title: Harp Strumming Riff 7.wav
415409.description:
Melodic Snippets from recordings of me playing the Swar SanGam. This wonderful instrument is a combination of the Swarmandal and the Tampura. 15 harp strings and 4 Drone/Bass strings. 
In these recordings I am only using the Swarmandal (Harp) part.
It is tuned to C sharp, but I have dropped the fourth note (F sharp) out of the scale.

There are four packs with lots of recordings in them, strums, plucks, short improvisations. 
"Short melodic statements" are 1-2 bars. "Riffs" are 2-4 bars. "Melodies" are about 30 seconds and "Runs and Flutters" speaks for itself. There is recording of tuning up the Swarmandal in the melodies pack.

The snippets were taken from recordings done on three different days so you may notice a slight difference in volume and background noise. A couple of the recordings have some ambient noise (bird tweets, wind chimes,)
Some of the melodies are based around a similar theme but have enough variation to be interesting/useful.

Credit is not required but always appreciated. Linking to the sound allows others to find this amazing website. :-)
I love to hear what you have used my sounds for!

415466.title: Harp Short Lovely.wav
415466.description:
Melodic Snippets from recordings of me playing the Swar SanGam. This wonderful instrument is a combination of the Swarmandal and the Tampura. 15 harp strings and 4 Drone/Bass strings. 
In these recordings I am only using the Swarmandal (Harp) part.
It is tuned to C sharp, but I have dropped the fourth note (F sharp) out of the scale.

There are four packs with lots of recordings in them, strums, plucks, short improvisations. 
"Short melodic statements" are 1-2 bars. "Riffs" are 2-4 bars. "Melodies" are about 30 seconds and "Runs and Flutters" speaks for itself. There is recording of tuning up the Swarmandal in the melodies pack.

The snippets were taken from recordings done on three different days so you may notice a slight difference in volume and background noise. A couple of the recordings have some ambient noise (bird tweets, wind chimes,)
Some of the melodies are based around a similar theme but have enough variation to be interesting/useful.

Credit is not required but always appreciated. Linking to the sound allows others to find this amazing website. :-)
I love to hear what you have used my sounds for!

410783.description:
First, I used the effect « noise decrease » to take the background noise out. This effect made the main sound clearer.
The effects “melt in opening” and “melt in closing time” made the sound smoother.
I also added a silence before and after the sound of the coin entering the coffee machine, in order to isolate it.
Finally, I “normalized” the sound.


_ _ _ _ _ _ _


TYPOLOGIE/MORPHOLOGIE DE SCHAEFFER

Je pense que ce son est une succession d’impulsions variées [V’].




Masse = Groupe nodal, alliance de plusieurs sons complexes.

Timbre harmonique = son terne et mécanique.

Dynamique = Le bruit de la pièce qui tombe dans la machine a une sonorité mécanique, ce qui explique la dynamique quelque peu abrupte de l’attaque du son.

410814.title: LIOTTARD_Alexandra_2017_2018_step.wav
410814.description:
This sound is created with a recording of step sound.
I have applicated a noise reduction on the base sound to eliminate the parasite noise. 
After that, I have added a fade in fade out.

Typologie/morphologie de P. Schaeffer
Il s’agit d’une itération complexe (X’’)
1- Masse :
Il s’agit d’un seul son complexe 
2- Timbre harmonique :
Nous pouvons dire qu’il s’agit d’un son relativement dynamique
3- Grain : 
En ce qui concerne le grain de ce son, nous ne pouvons pas dire qu’il est rugueux, mais nous ne pouvons pas dire qu’il est doux non plus. Il s’agit d’un son net.
4- Allure : 
Ce son ne comporte pas de vibrato
5- Dynamique : 
Le son démarre de façon abrupte au début, pour s’adoucir par la suite grâce au fondu de fermeture. Il est plutôt dynamique.
6- Profil mélodique :
Nous ne pouvons pas entendre de vraie différence de hauteur dans ce son, juste une diminution de la bande sonore de manière progressive.
7- Profil de masse :
Le son est calibré

410815.title: LIOTTARD_Alexandra_2017_2018_coinFall.wav
410815.description:
This sound is created with a recording of a coin insert in the coffee machine.
I have applicated a noise reduction on the base sound to eliminate the parasite noise. 
After that, I have added a fade in fade out.

Typologie/morphologie de P. Schaeffer
Ce son est composé d’impulsions complexes (X’)
1- Masse :
Il s’agit d’un seul son complexe
2- Timbre harmonique :
On peut dire que le timbre de ce son est métallique
3- Grain : 
Le son n’est pas totalement lisse, mais n’est pas rugueux. Nous pouvons dire qu’il fait plutôt penser à des frottements métalliques
4- Allure : 
Il n’y à pas de vibrato présent dans ce son, en revanche, nous pouvons entendre un très léger écho
5- Dynamique : 
L’attaque du son est relativement violente et abrupte. Durant toute la durée de l’extrait nous pouvons constater un certain dynamisme.
6- Profil mélodique :
Les variations entendues sont plutôt du genre serpentine.
7- Profil de masse :
Il y a une forme d’égalisation dans ce son.

415394.title: Harp Melody 9.wav
415394.description:
Melodic Snippets from recordings of me playing the Swar SanGam. This wonderful instrument is a combination of the Swarmandal and the Tanpura. 15 harp strings and 4 Drone/Bass strings. 
In these recordings I am only using the Swarmandal (Harp) part.
It is tuned to C sharp, but I have dropped the fourth note (F sharp) out of the scale.

There are four packs with lots of recordings in them; strums, plucks, short improvisations. 
"Short melodic statements" are 1-2 bars. "Riffs" are 2-4 bars. "Melodies" are about 30 seconds and "Runs and Flutters" is experimenting with running up and down the strings. There is recording of tuning up the Swarmandal in the melodies pack.

The snippets were taken from recordings done on three different days so you may notice a slight difference in volume and background noise. A couple of the recordings have some ambient noise (bird tweets, wind chimes,)
Some of the melodies are based around a similar theme but have enough variation to be interesting/useful.

Credit is not required but always appreciated. Linking to the sound allows others to find this amazing website. :-) 
I love to hear what you have used my sounds for!

415474.title: Harp Short 23.wav
415474.description:
Melodic Snippets from recordings of me playing the Swar SanGam. This wonderful instrument is a combination of the Swarmandal and the Tampura. 15 harp strings and 4 Drone/Bass strings. 
In these recordings I am only using the Swarmandal (Harp) part.
It is tuned to C sharp, but I have dropped the fourth note (F sharp) out of the scale.

There are four packs with lots of recordings in them, strums, plucks, short improvisations. 
"Short melodic statements" are 1-2 bars. "Riffs" are 2-4 bars. "Melodies" are about 30 seconds and "Runs and Flutters" speaks for itself. There is recording of tuning up the Swarmandal in the melodies pack.

The snippets were taken from recordings done on three different days so you may notice a slight difference in volume and background noise. A couple of the recordings have some ambient noise (bird tweets, wind chimes,)
Some of the melodies are based around a similar theme but have enough variation to be interesting/useful.

Credit is not required but always appreciated. Linking to the sound allows others to find this amazing website. :-)
I love to hear what you have used my sounds for!

414827.title: Gun Version 2 with forward bolt
414827.description:
This is the second version without the mechanical bolt. Maybe can be used for bolt action rifles.

Made this is ableton live, it is multilayered with the top end of a 9mm and the low end of an. Another carbine sound is faded in after the transients to give more sustain. Two reverbs fade in and out creating a smooth transition and blend. A little white noise is added for subtle sheen and air.

All the layers were grouped together into a single band compressor and ran through serum fx distortion and then into a krush distortion plugin for added fatness. A blending reverb was used to glue the sounds into the same space and ran into a final transient designer which is adding a little more snap and punch and clipping the excess transients off.

enjoy

404562.description:
I went for a more realistic gun sound without the Hollywood subbass and a lot cleaner than my previous work

Made in ableton live, i just layered an ak47, an m16, an enfield rifle and an acoustic kick drum together with eq and used parallel compression to gel them together. Transient designers were used on the layers to make them snap harder.

A bolt slide forward sample and a bolt slide back sample were added to give some mechanical feels to the gunshot.

enjoy

410848.description:
I recorded the sound of pieces in a coffee machine, and created a loop. I reduced the noise, add some reverberation.

Ce son est une itération variée (V"). Il est nodal, le timbre est terne, grave. Le grain est rugueux, l’attaque est plutôt forte. Le profil mélodique est composé de variations scalaires, le profil de masse est un profil « site ».

410840.title: RIVIERE_Anna_2017-2018-Casino jackpot.wav
410840.description:
To product this sound, I recorded the sound of a piece which has been put in a coffee machine.  We can hear the trajectory of the piece in the machine. To emphasize the piece’s sound, I first reduced the ambiant noise on Audacity. Then I modified the bass and treble and I added some silence at the beginning and at the end of the sound. I also used a leveler to make sure that we can clearly hear the moment when the piece is falling in the machine without having a saturation of the sound. 

The sound of the piece reminded me of the pieces which fall when we won something with a casino machine.

Typologie/Morphologie de P. Schaeffer 

Descriptif : Ce son est assez difficile à cerner, on perçoit du continu tonique (N') ainsi que des itérations toniques (N") et variées (V"). 

Masse: Il s’agit de sons cannelés puisqu'il y a un mélange de différents objets sonores.  

Grain : Le bruit est plutôt rugueux dès le début, on entend clairement à la suite une succession de notes rauques. Le grain est rocailleux et, on a l'impression d'entendre des sons qui semblent racler le bord d’une paroi. 

Dynamique : Le son est plutôt graduel, il y a une évolution du début à la fin, comme si nous assistions au mouvement d'un objet au sein d'un machine. 

Profil mélodique : Il s’agit d’une variation serpentine, on entend une succession de petites notes qui finissent par laisser place à un son final.

BsGr([fret position]f,[string number]s[MIDI note number])~v[velocity number 1-5]

166295.title: mco_walk_h04.wav
166295.description:
Footsteps...


NOTE: 

These are no field recordings but HANDMADE walking sounds in different speeds and manners intended for game creation. Most of them you can loop. They are recorded as dry as possible so you should add the ambience you like.  

HOW TO MAKE THESE:

1. First empty two bottles of the famous spanish brandy Lepanto.
2. Keep the korks - they have a very special sound different from the korks of wine bottles.
3. Then, if you're still able to hit (maybe you shouldn't drink the brandy alone and at once), fill things in a flat bowl or a plate - f. e. pepper grains or salt.
4. Step the korks in the bowl and record it. You may also - as I did - step the korks on other things like a ventilator.
5. Compress the sounds hard but limit them to -4 db (as they sound not naturally if they are to loud).

214885.title: The Big Squeak (13) So Week B
214885.description:
Okay, about this small bibliothek there is a story to tell.

Maybe a year ago my mother phoned me and asked if I could give her a hand because the door to her kitchen was squeaking. 
After work I went to her, went down to the cellar, took the can with the lubricating grease, went upstairs and made my mother happy. 
Then I putted the grease back and went upstairs again. Whe sat down, drank a cup of coffee. Then I had to go to the toilet and
noticed that the toilet door was squeaking too. So I went down to the cellar again and took once again the grease.

Now I thought, before I make the stairs again, I'll show if any other thing in my mothers house is squeaking. 

It was terrible! I swear, never in my entire life I've been in a house where so many different things were squeaking so impassionated.
First off all I went back to my car and took my cheap dictaphone I use for work. And before I putted grease on those squeaking things I recorded them.

xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx

So this are really historic sounds! None of them exist anymore in the real world!

xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx


But ... when I heard through them later I was disappointed of the bad sound quality, cutting out higher ond lower frenquencies of the rich spectrum of those "Neeeeiiiks" and "Uiihggs". 
During winter holidays I processed them first with the audacity noise reduction - then with other tools.

The result gives an unreal impression of the original sounding, they have now some "synthetic" touch - but makes them probably usable for funny films or comic-like effects.

All the sounds in my "big squeak pack" where recorded in one afternoon and all in my mothers house. The "tension-sounds" for example are nothing else than a junker (tin can? - sorry, my english) moved from one side of a wooden shelf to another, meanwhile my dictaphone was laying in the junker.


I don't ask to credit me - but if you make use of one of these sounds and create SOMETHING FUNNY with them, please let me know ... so I can show it my mother too.

Thank you.

92119.title: PPS13x3 E22 VELO07.wav
92119.description: This 48KHz/24bit sample pack, which is intended for use with software such as Drumagog or Sound Replacer, contains 121 samples of a Pearl Piccolo Steel 13x3 snare drum recorded with a choice of eleven different microphones and multiple velocity layers.  For each microphone choice there are eleven velocity layers.  The loudest strike is also a rimshot.  The microphones used were an AKG D202, an Audio Technica ATM250, an Audix D6, a Beyer Dynamic M201, an Electrovoice ND868, an Electrovoice RE20, a Josephson E22, a Lawson FET47, a Shure SM57 and a Shure SM7B.  The final microphone was the Josephson C720, a remarkable microphone of which only twenty were made to mark the Josephson company's 20th anniversary.  Placement of mic varied according to sensitivity and polar pattern.  Preamps used were Amek throughout and all sources were recorded directly to Pro Tools through Frontier Design Group and Digidesign converters.  Final editing and processing was carried out in Cool Edit Pro.

187042.title: Toriana G3.wav
187042.description:
In the basement of a house I found an old accordion with only the word Toriana on it. I recorded each of the white keys (the black ones didn't seem to work) and the sample name will tell you the note so that you can load it into a sampler. Because the accordion is old and falling apart each note sounds fairly different, and each sample includes first pulling the accordion apart and then pushing it back together. Sometimes those two actions create a slightly different sound.
This is by no means a pristine instrument, but it was recorded with a pair of AT4021 mics in XY stereo into a modified Marantz PMD661 and edited (simply each sample sliced) with Tracktion.

92082.title: PPS13x3 C720 VELO03.wav
92082.description: This 48KHz/24bit sample pack, which is intended for use with software such as Drumagog or Sound Replacer, contains 121 samples of a Pearl Piccolo Steel 13x3 snare drum recorded with a choice of eleven different microphones and multiple velocity layers.  For each microphone choice there are eleven velocity layers.  The loudest strike is also a rimshot.  The microphones used were an AKG D202, an Audio Technica ATM250, an Audix D6, a Beyer Dynamic M201, an Electrovoice ND868, an Electrovoice RE20, a Josephson E22, a Lawson FET47, a Shure SM57 and a Shure SM7B.  The final microphone was the Josephson C720, a remarkable microphone of which only twenty were made to mark the Josephson company's 20th anniversary.  Placement of mic varied according to sensitivity and polar pattern.  Preamps used were Amek throughout and all sources were recorded directly to Pro Tools through Frontier Design Group and Digidesign converters.  Final editing and processing was carried out in Cool Edit Pro.

84031.title: KBSD-M201-VELOCITY9.wav
84031.description: This sample pack contains 109 samples of a Ludwig Accent Combo 14x6 snare drum played by drummer Kent Breckner and recorded with eight different microphones and multiple velocity layers.  For each microphone there are ten velocity layers but in addition there is a ‘combi’ set which is a mixture of my three favorite mics with ten velocity layers and a ‘special’ set featuring those three mics with some processing and nineteen velocity layers, the even-numbered ones being interpolated.  The microphones used were a Shure SM57, a Beyer Dynamic M201, a Josephson e22s, a Josephson C42, a Neumann TLM103, an Electrovoice RE20, an Electrovoice ND868 and an Audio Technica Pro37R.  Placement of mic varied according to sensitivity and polar pattern.  Preamps used were NPNG and Millennia Media and all sources were recorded directly to Pro Tools through Frontier Design Group and Digidesign converters.  Final editing and processing was carried out in Cool Edit Pro.  This sample pack is intended for use with software such as Drumagog or Sound Replacer.

With no emotion, you just take out your portable recorder and record everything what he says, before other people (who want to sleep) begin to chase him away. Cesar Millan would say, that dogs usually express your energy, and sometimes try to help to release it. 93172.title: COKE CANS DISPOSAL C617 006.wav
93172.description: This 48KHz/24bit stereo sample pack contains 42 samples of various impacts, crushes and drops of empty coke cans and other artifacts in one of our tracking rooms.  There were about twenty coke cans, four plastic cups, a garbage pail and an empty Culligan water bottle.  These were arranged in various configurations and then kicked, dropped, smashed, crushed or otherwise mutilated.  The sources were recorded with four Josephson microphones — two C42s and two C617s — directly to Pro Tools through NPNG preamps.  Final edits were performed in Cool Edit Pro.  The C42s are directional and these recordings have been left 'as is'.  However most of the omnidirectional C617 tracks have been slowed down to half speed to give a much bigger sound.  Recorded by Zach Greenhorn and Reid Andreae at Pulsworks Audio Arts.

92529.title: TFUZ13x3 E22 VELO03.wav
92529.description: This 48KHz/24bit sample pack, which is intended for use with software such as Drumagog or Sound Replacer, contains 110 samples of a Tama Fuzzy 13x3 snare drum recorded with a choice of eleven different microphones and multiple velocity layers.  For each microphone choice there are ten velocity layers.  The microphones used were an AKG D202, an Audio Technica ATM250, an Audix D6, a Beyer Dynamic M201, an Electrovoice ND868, an Electrovoice RE20, a Josephson E22, a Lawson FET47, a Shure SM57 and a Shure SM7B.  The final microphone was the Josephson C720, a remarkable microphone of which only twenty were made to mark the Josephson company's 20th anniversary.  Placement of mic varied according to sensitivity and polar pattern.  Preamps used were Amek throughout and all sources were recorded directly to Pro Tools through Frontier Design Group and Digidesign converters.  Final editing and processing was carried out in Cool Edit Pro.

The microphones used were a a Josephson e22s, a Josephson C42, an Electrovoice ND868, an Audix D6, a Beyer Dynamic M69, an Audio Technica ATM-250 and an Audio Technica Pro37R. Preamps used were NPNG and Millennia Media and all sources were recorded directly to Pro Tools through Frontier Design Group and Digidesign converters. Final editing and processing was carried out in Cool Edit Pro. This sample pack is intended for use with software such as Drumagog or Sound Replacer.

56427.title: Kick-Coin-PlasticBeater-Medium2.wav
56427.description: These are samples I have recorded in my rehearsal room/studio. It's not a fancy studio, but it's something. Each drum is recorded with an SM57 on the top head and an SM58 on the resonant head, which have been mixed together with no phase issues. These samples are unprocessed, except for the kick drum which has had a slight boost in the 80hz region for about +3db to bring out that "in your chest" bass. The samples are originally intended to be used for blending in on recorded drums, hence why there aren't so many variations of the strokes, but I guess you could also use it for pure drum programming if you settle for a not so extremely dynamic and varied drum play/feel. Enjoy these samples, and keep up the good work everyone!

The files designated "FtSpl", "HO", "SO", and "O" are all 150,000 samples in length, and crossfade-looped with the loop range [100,000...149,999]. Samplers with .WAV file header support should automatically detect the loop range. Just enable looping, set the sample player's sustain parameter to 0% and use the decay and/or release parameter to fade the cymbals out to taste. A MIDI continuous-control number can be designated to modulate Amplitude Envelope Decay and/or Release parameters, as well as selection of the MIDI key to be triggered, corresponding to the strike zone/openness level of the instrument in appropriate hardware or software devices.

Notes for samples in this pack:

FtChk = Foot "Chick" sound (Pedal closes the cymbals and remains closed)

Foot-control types for stick strikes:

214877.title: The Big Speak (5) Cupboard
214877.description:
Okay, about this small bibliothek there is a story to tell.

Maybe a year ago my mother phoned me and asked if I could give her a hand because the door to her kitchen was squeaking. 
After work I went to her, went down to the cellar, took the can with the lubricating grease, went upstairs and made my mother happy. 
Then I putted the grease back and went upstairs. Whe sat down, drank a cup of coffee. Then I had to go to the toilet and
noticed that the toilet door was squeaking too. So I went down to the cellar again and took once again the grease.

Now I thought, before I make the stairs again, I'll show if any other thing in my mothers house is squeaking. 

It was terrible! I swear, never in my entire life I've been in a house where so many different things were squeaking so impassionated.
First off all I went back to my car and took my cheap dictaphone I use for work. And before I putted grease on those squeaking things I recorded them.

xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx

So this are really historic sounds! None of them exist anymore in the real world!

xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx


But ... when I heard through them later I was disappointed of the bad sound quality, cutting out higher ond lower frenquencies of the rich spectrum of those "Neeeeiiiks" and "Uiihggs". 
During winter holidays I processed them first with the audacity noise reduction - then with other tools.

The result gives an unreal impression of the original sounding, they have now some "synthetic" touch - but makes them probably usable for funny films or comic-like
effects.

All the sounds in my "big squeek pack" where recorded in one afternoon and all in my mothers house. The "tension-sounds" for example are nothing else than a junker (tin can? - sorry, my english) moved from one side of a wooden shelf to another, meanwhile my dictaphone was laying in the junker.


I don't ask to credit me - but if you make use of one of these sounds and create SOMETHING FUNNY with them, please let me know ... so I can show it my mother too.

Thank you.

First off all I went back to my car and took my cheap dictaphone I use for work. And before I putted grease on those squeaking things I recorded them.

xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx

So this are really historic sounds! None of them exist anymore in the real world!

xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx


But ... when I heard through them later I was disappointed of the bad sound quality, cutting out higher ond lower frenquencies of the rich spectrum of those "Neeeeiiiks" and "Uiihggs". 
During winter holidays I processed them first with the audacity noise reduction - then with other tools.

The result gives an unreal impression of the original sounding, they have now some "synthetic" touch - but makes them probably usable for funny films or comic-like
effects.

All the sounds in my "big squeek pack" where recorded in one afternoon and all in my mothers house. The "tension-sounds" for example are nothing else than a junker (tin can? - sorry, my english) moved from one side of a wooden shelf to another, meanwhile my dictaphone was laying in the junker.


I don't ask to credit me - but if you make use of one of these sounds and create SOMETHING FUNNY with them, please let me know ... so I can show it my mother too.

Thank you.

It is a dark and moody sounding, a lot of character but in now way "pristine".

Notes for samples in this pack:

Tuning:
VLP = Very Low Pitch
LP = Low Pitch
MLP = Medium-Low Pitch
MP = Medium Pitch
MHP = Medium-High Pitch
HP = High Pitch
VHP = Very High Pitch

Playing style:
CS = Cross Stick Strike (Shank of stick strikes the rim while the butt of the stick rests on the head)
HdC = Head-Center Strike
HdE = Head-Edge Strike
RS = Rimshot (Simultaneous head and rim) Strike
Rm = Rim Strike

Snare Strainer settings:
0Sn = Snares off
LSn = Loose Snares
TSn = Tight Snares

Velocity:
v## =the number designation for the velocity with which the instrument was played

92365.title: CLOSE FEMALE LAUGH 006.wav
92365.description: This 48KHz/24bit sample pack contains 49 samples of close-mic'd female laughter.  A well-known author visited the studio to record the 'audio book' version of her novel for her publisher.  During the 16 hours (!) it took to record the 90,000 word story we got on really well and our jolly banter made it onto the unedited tracks.  The author has given me permission to keep and share her laughter as long as I don't release her identity.  Recorded with the incredible Josephson C720 microphone through NPNG preamp and Empirical Labs compression.  Tracked to Pro Tools with final edits performed in Cool Edit Pro.  At some points my voice may be heard through the talkback and there are some movement noises and paper shuffling etc.  There is also the occasional spoken word.  I'm not sure why some of these samples are clipped to snot; probably a Pro Tools gremlin.  Still, it doesn't sound too bad.

92074.title: PPS13x3 ATM250 VELO06.wav
92074.description: This 48KHz/24bit sample pack, which is intended for use with software such as Drumagog or Sound Replacer, contains 121 samples of a Pearl Piccolo Steel 13x3 snare drum recorded with a choice of eleven different microphones and multiple velocity layers.  For each microphone choice there are eleven velocity layers.  The loudest strike is also a rimshot.  The microphones used were an AKG D202, an Audio Technica ATM250, an Audix D6, a Beyer Dynamic M201, an Electrovoice ND868, an Electrovoice RE20, a Josephson E22, a Lawson FET47, a Shure SM57 and a Shure SM7B.  The final microphone was the Josephson C720, a remarkable microphone of which only twenty were made to mark the Josephson company's 20th anniversary.  Placement of mic varied according to sensitivity and polar pattern.  Preamps used were Amek throughout and all sources were recorded directly to Pro Tools through Frontier Design Group and Digidesign converters.  Final editing and processing was carried out in Cool Edit Pro.

137462.title: HH13inKZ-ESO~v09.wav
137462.description:
A 1-shot sample taken of a 13-inch diameter Zildjian K/Z HiHat cymbal pair (K-series top cymbal and Z-Custom bottom cymbal), recorded with an MXL 603 close-mic and two Peavey electret condenser microphones in an XY pair. The files designated "FtSpl", "HO", "SO", and "O" are all 150,000 samples in length, and crossfade-looped with the loop range [100,000...149,999]. Samplers with .WAV file header support should automatically detect the loop range. Just enable looping, set the sample player's sustain parameter to 0% and use the decay and/or release parameter to fade the cymbals out to taste. A MIDI continuous-control number can be designated to modulate Amplitude Envelope Decay and/or Release parameters, as well as selection of the MIDI key to be triggered, corresponding to the strike zone/openness level of the instrument in appropriate hardware or software devices.

Notes for samples in this pack:

Playing style:

Cymbal strike types:

Bl = Bell Strike
Bw = Bow Strike
E = Edge Strike
FtChk = Foot "Chick" sound (Pedal closes the cymbals and remains closed)
FtSpl = Foot "Splash" sound (Pedal closes the cymbals and is immediately released for the cymbals to decay naturally)

Foot-control types for stick strikes:

Cl = Tightly Closed
SC = Semi-Closed
HO = Half-Open
SO = Semi-Open
O = Fully Open

Velocity:
v## =the number designation for the velocity with which the instrument was played

92389.title: CLOSE FEMALE LAUGH 030.wav
92389.description: This 48KHz/24bit sample pack contains 49 samples of close-mic'd female laughter.  A well-known author visited the studio to record the 'audio book' version of her novel for her publisher.  During the 16 hours (!) it took to record the 90,000 word story we got on really well and our jolly banter made it onto the unedited tracks.  The author has given me permission to keep and share her laughter as long as I don't release her identity.  Recorded with the incredible Josephson C720 microphone through NPNG preamp and Empirical Labs compression.  Tracked to Pro Tools with final edits performed in Cool Edit Pro.  At some points my voice may be heard through the talkback and there are some movement noises and paper shuffling etc.  There is also the occasional spoken word.  I'm not sure why some of these samples are clipped to snot; probably a Pro Tools gremlin.  Still, it doesn't sound too bad.

137514.title: HH13inKZ-BwSC-v15.wav
137514.description:
A 1-shot sample taken of a 13-inch diameter Zildjian K/Z HiHat cymbal pair (K-series top cymbal and Z-Custom bottom cymbal), recorded with an MXL 603 close-mic and two Peavey electret condenser microphones in an XY pair. The files designated "FtSpl", "HO", "SO", and "O" are all 150,000 samples in length, and crossfade-looped with the loop range [100,000...149,999]. Samplers with .WAV file header support should automatically detect the loop range. Just enable looping, set the sample player's sustain parameter to 0% and use the decay and/or release parameter to fade the cymbals out to taste. A MIDI continuous-control number can be designated to modulate Amplitude Envelope Decay and/or Release parameters, as well as selection of the MIDI key to be triggered, corresponding to the strike zone/openness level of the instrument in appropriate hardware or software devices.

Notes for samples in this pack:

Playing style:

Cymbal strike types:

Bl = Bell Strike
Bw = Bow Strike
E = Edge Strike
FtChk = Foot "Chick" sound (Pedal closes the cymbals and remains closed)
FtSpl = Foot "Splash" sound (Pedal closes the cymbals and is immediately released for the cymbals to decay naturally)

Foot-control types for stick strikes:

Cl = Tightly Closed
SC = Semi-Closed
HO = Half-Open
SO = Semi-Open
O = Fully Open

Velocity:
v## =the number designation for the velocity with which the instrument was played

165444.title: HMS_7.wav
165444.description: These plucked-strings-like sounds were created with the technique invented and developed in my PhD, called Histogram Mapping Synthesis (HMS). HMS is based on Cellular Automata (CA) which are mathematical/computational models that create moving images. In the context of HMS, these images are analysed by histogram measurements, giving as a result a sequence of histograms. In a nutshell, these histogram sequences are converted into spectrograms which in turn are rendered into sounds. Additional DSP methods were developed to control the CA and the synthesis so as to be able to design and produce sounds in a predictable and controllable manner. For further reading, see: http://cmr.soc.plymouth.ac.uk/publications/AES10.pdf

236942.description: This is a Gerber brand toilet at 1.28 Gallons Per Flush, 4.8 Liters Per Flush. Don't know what you can use it for, but I'm sure you can use it. I bought a brand new Sony model ICD-LX330 digital memory card recorder. It records onto SDHC cards. It has dual stereo left and right mics on it for good recording. The mics are VERY high quality. 211203.description:
Assymetric ticking noise. Sounds like the ticking of an analogue counter.

A single clock tick was placed on two seperate tracks in order to control the time interval between ticks. One of the tracks was pitch shifted to create the sound of two, slightly different ticks. Both tracks pass through a tight chorus filter and a delay tap to recreate a slight sense of springiness and rattle as the "counter wheels" tick over.

Created in FLStudio with one audio clip, FruityDelay2, Fruity FastDist, Fruity Parametric EQ 2, Fruity Chorus and EQUO.

239823.description:
A 1-shot sample taken of a finger-plucked Gretsch Electromatic 30.3" (77 cm) scale length bass guitar, recorded direct-to-disk. 

Notes for samples in this pack:

The note performances are from various fret positions across the playing range of the instrument. Each position has 8 velocity layers per note.

Naming conventions for note samples is as follows:

BsGr([fret position]f,[string number]s[MIDI note number])~v[velocity number 1-5]

Fret positions with the designation [N#] indicate "negative fret", which are samples of the low E string detuned down in relation to their open standard-tuned (unfretted) note.

The note performance samples contain a crossfade-looped region at the end of each file. Samplers with .WAV file header support should automatically detect the loop range. Just enable looping, set the sample player's sustain parameter to 0% and use the decay parameter to fade the sample out as needed. Loop regions begin at sample 200,000 and end at sample 299,999.

166304.title: mco_walk_f01.wav
166304.description:
Footsteps...


NOTE: 

These are no field recordings but HANDMADE walking sounds in different speeds and manners intended for game creation. Most of them you can loop. They are recorded as dry as possible so you should add the ambience you like.  

HOW TO MAKE THESE:

1. First empty two bottles of the famous spanish brandy Lepanto.
2. Keep the korks - they have a very special sound different from the korks of wine bottles.
3. Then, if you're still able to hit (maybe you shouldn't drink the brandy alone and at once), fill things in a flat bowl or a plate - f. e. pepper grains or salt.
4. Step the korks in the bowl and record it. You may also - as I did - step the korks on other things like a ventilator.
5. Compress the sounds hard but limit them to -4 db (as they sound not naturally if they are to loud).

56435.description: These are samples I have recorded in my rehearsal room/studio. It's not a fancy studio, but it's something. These samples are unprocessed, except for the kick drum which has had a slight boost in the 80hz region for about +3db to bring out that "in your chest" bass. The samples are originally intended to be used for blending in on recorded drums, hence why there aren't so many variations of the strokes, but I guess you could also use it for pure drum programming if you settle for a not so extremely dynamic and varied drum play/feel. Enjoy these samples, and keep up the good work everyone!

250654.description:
HOW I DID IT? --------------------------
Using 3 tracks mixed together: 
First track (3 seconds)
Generate a sound (sinus) : frequency 440 hz - Amplitude 0,8 – duration 3 seconds 
apply effects : Wha-wha = frequency 2,2 – Phase of departure 320 - Depth 23% - Echo 5,3 – Gap of frequency 22%. 
Second track generate a sound (sinus) : frequency 440 hz - Amplitude 0,8 – duration 3 seconds
Export this two tracks together and open it in a new file. 
Then generate the third track
Generate a whistle sound (sinus) starting at 440hz finishing at 1320hz (logarythmic interpolation /3 seconds)
duplicate the sound on the same track but paste it in inverse sense. 
On the first audio track, cross the sound to the left, then to the right for the second audio track. 

HOW CAN I DESCRIBE IT? (French)----------------------

92266.title: MPM14x5½ FET47 VELO4.wav
92266.description: This 48KHz/24bit sample pack, which is intended for use with software such as Drumagog or Sound Replacer, contains 99 samples of a Mapex Pro-M 14x5½ snare drum recorded with a choice of eleven different microphones and multiple velocity layers.  For each microphone choice there are nine velocity layers.  The microphones used were an AKG D202, an Audio Technica ATM250, an Audix D6, a Beyer Dynamic M201, an Electrovoice ND868, an Electrovoice RE20, a Josephson E22, a Lawson FET47, a Shure SM57 and a Shure SM7B.  The final microphone was the Josephson C720, a remarkable microphone of which only twenty were made to mark the Josephson company's 20th anniversary.  Placement of mic varied according to sensitivity and polar pattern.  Preamps used were Amek throughout and all sources were recorded directly to Pro Tools through Frontier Design Group and Digidesign converters.  Final editing and processing was carried out in Cool Edit Pro.

183023.description:
A 1-shot sample taken of a Yamaha Eterna classical acoustic guitar, recorded with a CAD E100 microphone. 

Notes for samples in this pack:

Included are both finger-plucked note performances, and fingered fret noise effects. The note performances are from various fret positions across the playing range of the instrument. Each position has 5 velocity layers per note.

Naming conventions for note samples is as follows:

92271.title: MPM14x5½ FET47 VELO9.wav
92271.description: This 48KHz/24bit sample pack, which is intended for use with software such as Drumagog or Sound Replacer, contains 99 samples of a Mapex Pro-M 14x5½ snare drum recorded with a choice of eleven different microphones and multiple velocity layers.  For each microphone choice there are nine velocity layers.  The microphones used were an AKG D202, an Audio Technica ATM250, an Audix D6, a Beyer Dynamic M201, an Electrovoice ND868, an Electrovoice RE20, a Josephson E22, a Lawson FET47, a Shure SM57 and a Shure SM7B.  The final microphone was the Josephson C720, a remarkable microphone of which only twenty were made to mark the Josephson company's 20th anniversary.  Placement of mic varied according to sensitivity and polar pattern.  Preamps used were Amek throughout and all sources were recorded directly to Pro Tools through Frontier Design Group and Digidesign converters.  Final editing and processing was carried out in Cool Edit Pro.

102391.title: IMPROV PERCS 054 2 BARS 130 BPM.wav
102391.description: This 48KHz/24bit stereo sample pack contains 71 loops (77Mb) of improvised percussion instruments at 130BPM.  Sources were placed on the studio floor and played with two regular drumsticks.  A central AKG C414 in omni config through NPNG preamp was the closest mic but in some cases an Audio Technica contact mic was also used.  Two Josephson C617s through Millennia Media preamps captured the room ambience.  Sources included water bottles, large vacuum cleaner pipes, a steel speaker stand, food containers and various other objects which were never meant to be used like this.  All sources were recorded into Pro Tools through Frontier Design Group converters and large amounts of Beat Detective were employed to make something decent out of my terrible playing.  Final processing was carried out in Cool Edit Pro.  Recorded by Brady Leduc at Pulsworks Audio Arts.

324579.title: DE_LIMA_LUCIO_Romain_2015_2016_revolving_light.wav
324579.description:
To realize that sound I usead a sinuosidal whistle of 150 Hz generated by Audacity.
Then I duplicated it and reversed the second part. Then, I duplicated the result a few times to get a first track.
Then I duplicated this track 3 times and desynchronysed every track by 3,33 seconds from the previous one, just to give the impression that there were several police cars.

Type de son : Continu Varié (V)
Je trouve ce son éclatant et strident, car il fait bien sur penser au gyrophare de la police, qui est un objet lumineux, et qui n'est pas conçu pour être agréable mais plutot pour être audible.
Le son est parfaitement lisse et ne comporte pas de vibrato. L'attaque du son est abrupte. Les variations sont graduelles, glissantes, il n'y a jamais de véritables ruptures.Le son n'est pas filtré et n'a pas subi d'équalisation.
